explanation: The two-job execution is faulty because the top-level corpus contains record n06-r01 with demand_score 9, so it qualifies under the stipulated score-threshold selection and should be preserved. Job 1 output omits n06-r01 from both needs and evidence_sources, and Job 2 receives only the already-omitted seven-record handoffs, so the downstream result reflects an upstream omission. The supplied function evidence localizes the omission to normalize: its allowed_record_ids list excludes n06-r01 and includes n06-r09 instead, causing retained_df to filter out the qualifying record after select_demand would have selected it.
cited_evidence: Top-level input includes {'record_id':'n06-r01','need':'isolate faulty execution branches before replay','demand_score':9,'source_id':'s01','source_weight':5}.
Behavioural criteria require selecting all qualifying or fallback demand records and preserving record_id, need, demand_score, source_id, and source_weight.
Job 1 output needs and evidence_sources contain n06-r02 through n06-r08 only; metadata record_count and evidence_source_count are 7.
select_demand source selects rows where demand_score >= 3 or record_id is in fallback_ids, which would include n06-r01.
normalize source sets allowed_record_ids to ['n06-r09','n06-r02','n06-r03','n06-r04','n06-r05','n06-r06','n06-r07','n06-r08'] and filters retained_df by those IDs, excluding n06-r01.
Job 2 input needs and evidence_sources exactly match the seven-record Job 1 handoff, so the missing n06-r01 was already absent before downstream processing.
